title: Best app I’ve ever bought
body:
I have for months been resigning myself to the fact that I probably just need to get a dumb phone to curb social media and YouTube’s impact on my life and time. Then this app came into my awareness and changed everything. Truly, if you’re worried about screen time, this is the app for you. 

The setup instructions are easy to follow and I can’t believe what a difference it’s made in the last month or so since I bought it. I went from hours of scrolling to…maybe half an hour a day maximum? The interventions are just inconvenient and effective enough to really work, and having to write my intention for using social media every time is a game changer.  At night, I put it on a reoccurring strict mode and it’s also revolutionized my sleep. No more getting sucked down late night YouTube rabbit holes. 

It is exactly what I’ve been wanting and I’m so grateful I found it 🙏 truly, if you’re also struggling, get this app. It’s more than worth your money for the full version

title: Just try it!
body:
I was skeptical but, the app was free so I gave it a shot. After an adjustment period where I kept being SUPER annoyed & changing settings constantly, it high key started to work. In fact it worked so well I went from wasting at my peak 8 hours of my life on an app I felt trapped on to deleting Instagram after nearly 12 years of almost daily use. I’ve now re-downloaded Instagram with little to no restrictions placed on it & I still don’t want to use it anymore.

Yes it took awhile, for me it was about 9 months. I upgraded to premium maybe 4 months in to utilize the “re-interventions” feature, this isn’t a quick fix but, trust me the constant interruptions are training your brain no matter how you respond to them. I even found what many are saying is a “glitch” where the intervention takes 5 seconds to pop-up letting you catch a glimpse of the app you’re trying to open was good because usually, the dumb reel I suffered through the intervention to see wasn’t worth it & I started hating social media for that! 

I also appreciate that the updates they post explain bug fixes in plain language & the instructions for how to set up interventions are similar. The app has no forced ads that are bothersome, except for their paywall and it doesn’t limit the usefulness of the app it just kind of limits how many tools you can utilize & is slightly annoying to exit out of which I found to be pretty reasonable. I was even offered a discount when I did finally get premium, which was great. Its refreshing to finally have an app that seems like it’s trying to actually provide a helpful service first & foremost, instead of focusing mostly on being profitable to the detriment of the user. 

So yeah thanks to the whole app team ya’ll are doing a great thing (& your marketing clearly isn’t too shabby either), so far I have regained about 4.8 weeks of my life thanks to you & the power of annoyance.

title: I hate how well this works.
body:
I’ve only been using this app for about a week, and yet I’ve already noticed that the time spent on my target app is greatly reduced. It really does make you stop and think about what’s really important to you in the moment. And the forced breathing exercise is so annoying (as it’s supposed to be) that I’m noticing I’m not even trying to open the app half as often as I normally would. Also, being told how many times you’ve tried to open the app in a 24 hour period really puts things in to perspective. My compulsive scrolling habits were so much worse than I thought they were, but I’m seeing improvement already! Watching the number of attempts go down over time is quite satisfying.

If you do need to switch away from the app for a moment it is annoying in the free version to have to go through the exercise again, but the intentional app switching feature in pro helps. Of course, if you don’t actually have a reason to need to come back right away, making it annoying on purpose is good too.

title: Good for the impatient or busy, ineffective if you’re willing to wait
body:
I started using onesec via their Firefox extension, which lets you configure as many sites as you want, and I use the free version of onesec to block the Safari extension as a whole, as I deleted all my social media apps a while ago and access them via browser. 

I have my browser extension set to 30 seconds, displaying a version of the “Litany Against Fear” quote edited to be about scrolling, and my phone app is configured to 20 seconds. To a lesser being, this long wait time may be enough to starve out your app-opening impulse. I am, however, a persistence hunter of the desire to waste time. onesec is perfect for me not in that it redirects me away from my impulse to use Twitter or other social media — all it does is let me waste 20-30 seconds (more like 30-40, the breathing animation lasts a small percentage longer than you set it) more than I would otherwise have on social media. 

This isn’t an issue exclusive to onesec, and I assume this app is very useful if you have a brain that wants to cooperate with you to reduce your social media usage. Unfortunately, I’m too accustomed to circumventing roadblocks between me and my next tweet, so I will have to look elsewhere for a weapon strong enough for me.

title: Legitimately Life Changing
body: One sec says it's saved me hours in a few weeks, but it only counts preventing an open as saving 3 minutes. With how I was spending time on my app vices before the app, I know I've gotten back LITERAL DAYS of my precious mortal life. Premium is more than worth it and I appreciate a non-subscription model. I do wish very much that I could set multiple time spans for the "back to reality" reminders. 3 minutes is fine for instagram, but way too short for YouTube, for example. And once I ignore the first reminder, there's nothing else ever until I leave the app again on my own. If I could have reminders at 3, 5, 10 and 30 minutes, for example, the accountability would continue, and it would seem like a simple add to the app's functionality. Even better would be different reminder times for different apps, but just being able to pick more than one time span would be spectacular and help with the last issue I'm dealing with in app usage.

So when I it stops me from opening it works, but once I have it open I think I stay on longer (kinda like revenge scrolling).

Again an issue with me not the app! If there was some way to mitigate this issue I would definitely be purchasing premium! Maybe the an option to have the app force close every few minutes? Or when you turn off your phone the app makes you redo the wait screen time? I’m not sure!

body: Takes a lot of work to set up and won’t work on my shopping apps because I can’t select them for the shortcut.  Really wanted something that will wean me off screen time slowly. Should be helpful for mindfulness for the apps it does work for.
author: brameg

title: Perfect solution!
body: Works a lot better than setting up screen times in your iPhone settings. The deep breath and countdown truly allows you to think about why you’re opening the app, and prevents mindless scrolling. I’ve recommended this app to everyone I know, especially those who resort to deleting social media when it takes up too much time. This is a much more efficient solution. Thank you!

title: Excellent!
body: I sometimes have a reflex to open social media on my phone without purpose. This wonderful app makes me take a beat, and a breath, to rethink if I really wanted to open the app or not.

title: What an inspired idea!
body: This app takes Apple’s screen time to the next level. I’m also amazed how people keep leveraging Shortcuts to do clever things like this. Buy this app if you want a better approach to limiting social media time than is baked into iOS.
